title: 4 Million People Watched a Robot Find 57 New Species

scenes.text: Four million people watched a robot find 57 new species. Live.
A robot sub dived into a canyon off Argentina, almost twice as deep as the Grand Canyon.
A mile and a half down, a sea cucumber with horns. They named it Loki.
An orange starfish that looked like Patrick went viral. It wasn't even new.
They checked one in ten of the tiny crustaceans caught. Every one was new.
Fifty-seven new species, most samples still unchecked. Four million watched. We've barely started looking.

description:
More than four million people watched live as a robot submarine explored a deep-sea canyon off Argentina, and scientists have now confirmed 57 new species from the dives.
The Mar del Plata Canyon drops below 3,500 metres, nearly twice the depth of the Grand Canyon. The haul includes a horned sea cucumber nicknamed Loki found 2,577 metres down, 22 new echinoderms, 14 new corals and 20 new copepods; the bright orange sea star that went viral as Patrick turned out not to be new. The names were settled at a two-week workshop in Buenos Aires in July 2026 and announced in October 2026.
If you could name one of the new species, what would you call it?
first_comment: The starfish that went viral wasn't a new species, but the horned sea cucumber was. Which would you rather have named after you: a starfish or a sea cucumber?
